how_predicted: predict_script_a.py integrates A in NumPy with 0.2's update rules and with 0.3's, the drag model shared. With 0.2's rules it reproduces the reference (validation below); each of 0.3's changes is then made alone and together. The predicted 0.3 values are that emulation's, in float64; float32's are the f32 reference moved by the emulated difference.

differences.reasoning: 0.2's graph adds the magnet node before the body, on the loop body -> magnet -> body, so body.orientation -> magnet.orientation reads the previous step, as 0.3's umr.pose -> magnetic.torque:umr.pose does. Both measured lags therefore contain -omega dt. Settled before the run from the surrogate's rotational resistance about the tube's axis where the body rests (with lubrication): see operating_point. With the previous orientation, the measured lag is arcsin(R omega / m B) - omega dt; with this step's, arcsin(R omega / m B) alone. The reference's lag is the first to within the steady translation's coupling, and 0.03 rad from the second. The emulation, which reads the previous orientation, reproduces the reference's lag to rounding.
differences.check: test_script_a_lag_structure.py asserts the declared mapping of the two graphs' edges

differences.what: drag: 0.2's explicit drag from the previous step against 0.3's implicit resistance, with the body confined by projection
differences.reasoning: Expected beforehand: no change in the steady quantities while locked. At A's operating point that does not hold. The body rests on the wall, and each step 0.3's implicit solve gives it the outward velocity of a fall, about dt F/m (F the buoyant weight and the outward hydrodynamic load), which the projection then removes: but the solve has already resisted that velocity, so the resistance's column along the wall's normal adds a load the body never feels (to the axial force and, through the end-referenced coupling MIME-ANO-112 records, to the tilting torques). The emulation leaves 0.0014 m/s outward for the projection each step (dt times the buoyant weight over the mass: 0.00143 m/s). 0.2's drag reads the velocity after the projection and never sees the fall. The error is first order in dt: the gap halves as dt halves, and both schemes meet as dt -> 0 (convergence). Predicted: the swim speed +2.352%, the lag -6.308e-06 rad, the body's rotation rate -4.92e-09. The control: with the contact held in the solve (the velocity along the normal set to zero inside it), 0.3's scheme gives -0.110% at this dt instead, the remaining difference between implicit and explicit resistance.
differences.transient: differs: over the first 0.5 s, the speed by displacement changes by +2.38%

differences.what: the 0.2 projection removed only (R/r)^2 of the outward velocity
differences.reasoning: On the floor the step overshoots the wall by about dt times the outward velocity u (operating_point), so 1 - (R/r)^2 is about 2 dt u / R, and the reference's body kept that fraction of u, outward, into the next step's explicit drag. Predicted: the swim speed -3.51e-05, the lag +1.1e-08 rad, the rotation rates under 1e-10.

differences.what: found in the mapping: when the drag reads the body's position
differences.reasoning: 0.2's surrogate read the position at the start of the step before (a back edge), its lubrication the position after the body's step (a forward edge); 0.3's one node reads the start of the step. On the wall the offset is the constraint's radius at every step, and the surrogate depends on the offset alone, so only the offset's direction moves between those reads (about 1e-4 rad a step). Inside the integrator's emulation, not separable from it.

lag_structure.rule: inside a loop, an edge whose source is scheduled at or after its target reads the previous step; a previous-step read is planned when it carries a thing's published state (mime.build._lags)

field.field_gradient -> magnet.field_gra.relation: dropped: 0.3's torque law reads no gradient (a gradient's force is another law's; the uniform field's is zero)

body.orientation -> magnet.orientation.relation: same: the torque reads the orientation at the start of the step

body.velocity -> mlp_drag.body_velocity.relation: dropped: it fed the surrogate's own drag, which the lubrication node's replaced; 0.3 delivers the resistance, which the body applies to the velocity it solves for

magnet.magnetic_force -> body.magnetic_f.relation: same (one wrench carries force and torque)

mlp_drag.resistance_matrix -> lub.resist.relation: merged: the surrogate and the lubrication are one node in 0.3

body.position -> lub.robot_position.relation: differs: 0.2's lubrication read the position after the body's step, 0.3's the start of the step

body.velocity -> lub.body_velocity.relation: differs: 0.2's drag took the velocity after the step and the body applied it in the next; 0.3's resistance is applied to the velocity the body's implicit solve gives

lub.drag_force -> body.drag_force.relation: differs: a delivered load read a step late (explicit drag) becomes a resistance read this step and applied implicitly

drive:field.amplitude.value -> field.mag.why: 0.2's commands were external inputs, built as float32 by its controller; 0.3's are constant drives

drag:umr.background_load -> umr.backgrou.why: the load of the ambient flow on the held body: zero in quiescent water

umr.twist -> swim_speed:umr.twist.why: an observation: 0.2's speed was computed from its history afterwards

post_hoc.found: on the first run of the float32 comparison (4c2d532): the phase lag missed its tolerance, -2.22e-7 rad against 1e-7, while the other four float32 quantities held and every float64 quantity held to 1e-14
post_hoc.what: 0.3's implicit step quantizes the locked torque balance in float32
post_hoc.reasoning: The step solves (M/dt + R) V' = (M/dt) V + F: about the tube's axis the inertial term (I/dt) omega, 1.298e-05 N m, carries the torque m B sin(phi), about 3.9e-8 N m, and float32 rounds their sum at one unit in the last place, 9.09e-13 N m. Locked, omega is the same at every step, so the rounding is the same at every step and the lock absorbs it as a fixed lag offset of up to that unit over m B cos(phi): 4.51e-07 rad. 0.2's explicit step rounds the same balance at a unit of omega, 3.91e-07 rad of lag (its realized offset, -8.5e-9 rad, lay well inside). The declared float32 tolerance on the lag, ten times the reference's realized float32-float64 gap, took that one draw for the resolution; the resolution is the quantization, above the tolerance.

with_the_step_solved_for_the_change_in_v.form: (M/dt + R) dV = F - R V, V' = V + dV: the same equation

post_hoc.what: rigid_inertial 0.2.0, as first written, holds the contact by correcting the twist after the step: V'_held = (V + dV) - lambda A^-1 N, two float32 roundings at a unit in the last place of the large twist (omega = 62.8 rad/s) with a small correction between them
post_hoc.reasoning: Locked, the same roundings recur at every step and stay in the lag, as MIME-ANO-113's did: the increment form only helps if the small increment is added to the twist once. Measured before this declaration, over six field amplitudes 1.2 mT x (1 + 2.5e-4 k), which move where the locked balance sits on the float32 grid and not the physics: with change 1's scheme the float32 lag sits within 4e-9 rad of float64 at every draw (the old form: -2.2e-7 to -2.7e-7); with the hold (changes 1 and 2) -2.8e-8 to -3.3e-8; with the shift (changes 1 and 3) -0.5e-8 to -1.5e-8; with all three -1.5e-7 to -1.7e-7, systematic, not a draw. The hold's correction is larger with the resistance about the centre, whose coupling carries the fall's correction into the turning about the axis. Proposed: correct the increment, V' = V + (dV - lambda A^-1 N), the same equation, so float64 moves by rounding only.

declared_changes.reasoning: The same equation, so in float64 A moves only by rounding: the emulated change is below (effect_of_this_change), and it is declared within 1e-12 relative on the speeds and rates and 1e-12 rad on the lag, a few thousand units in the last place over 10000 steps of a locked (contracting) lag. In float32 the small load is no longer added to the inertial term (I/dt) omega before the solve, so the lock's fixed rounding offset in the lag goes: 4c2's diagnostic run of this form measured the float32 lag +3.97e-9 rad from the float64 lag, against -2.32e-7 with the old form. The float32 lag is therefore gated again, against the f32 reference moved by the declared difference, at its original tolerance, 1e-7 rad, and the post hoc exemption (post_hoc[0]) is withdrawn.
